brief.goal: Agree the two referral moves we fund next
brief.takeaway: Referrals stall at the ask, not at the relationship

slides.name: Cover
slides.story: Sets the room: this is a working review of referral growth, not a status update.
slides.headline: Growing partnerships through referrals
slides.subtitle: Partnership growth review

slides.name: Agenda
slides.story: Frames the session in one sentence and names the four stops so nobody waits for their topic.
slides.headline: We agree where referral growth comes from and what we change next
slides.message: Four stops, one decision at the end

items.text: Why referrals: the conversion gap we are leaving on the table
Where they stall: three moments, each with a different fix
What the data says: two channels carry the volume
What we decide: two moves, one owner each

slides.name: Where referrals stall
slides.story: Names the three failure modes so the room stops arguing about whether partners care.
slides.message: Partners do not forget to refer; the ask never happens
slides.headline: Referrals stall at three moments, and each one has a different fix
slides.notes: Ask the room which of the three they recognise before showing the takeaway bar.

items.body: Partners meet the right person weeks before they think of us. Nothing in the meeting flow prompts an introduction, so the moment goes by.
When the moment comes, partners describe us in their own words. The introduction lands flat and the other side cannot tell why it matters.
Introductions arrive in a partner inbox and sit there. Nobody owns the first reply, so a warm lead cools to the temperature of a cold one.

content.text: Fix the ask, not the relationship: a scripted moment beats another reminder email

slides.name: The prize
slides.story: Sizes the opportunity with three numbers the team already trusts, so the fix is worth funding.
slides.message: A warm introduction is worth four cold ones
slides.headline: A warm introduction converts four times better than a cold list

items.label: Of new partners came from a referral
Shorter from first contact to signed

paragraphs: The gap is not interest. Partners who refer once refer again within the quarter, and their introductions close faster than outbound leads.
Every point of referral share we win is a point we stop buying.

slides.name: The ask moment
slides.story: Shows the scripted moment as a table the team can adopt on Monday, beside the four conditions that make it work.
slides.message: Script the moment and name the owner
slides.headline: Partners ask when the moment is scripted, not when reminded

items.text: One moment per partner journey, not a campaign
Words the partner already uses, written down
A named owner for the first reply

slides.name: Where growth comes from
slides.story: Puts the channel mix on screen so the funding argument is about two channels, not six.
slides.headline: Two channels drive nine of every ten introductions

paragraphs: Existing partners grew 38% this year while events fell.
Advisors are small but convert at twice the rate.
Fund the two that compound; stop staffing the rest.

content.text: If asked about events: the drop is deliberate, we cut two sponsorships.

slides.name: The referral flow
slides.story: Shows the scripted ask as one diagram, so the room can see where the owner changes.
slides.headline: four steps turn a warm moment into a signed referral

content.text: The owner changes at the hand-off, which is where referrals go cold

slides.name: The ask
slides.story: Closes on the decision: pick two moves, name owners, leave with a date-free commitment.
slides.message: Pick two moves and name the owners
slides.headline: Pick the two moves we fund this quarter and name an owner for each

content.text: We never stopped wanting to refer you. Nobody ever asked us at a moment when it was easy.

content.label: Designed next-steps strip: Decide, Fund, Assign, Review
